The privilege was never declared, so no role could be granted it. Only superusers, who bypass privilege checks, could generate the visit summary.

**Why it happened:** `VisitSummaryPdfReport.generatePdf` calls `Context.requirePrivilege(VIEW_VISIT_SUMMARY)`, where the constant is `"App: Can generate a Visit Summary"` (`openmrs-module-patientdocuments/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/patientdocuments/reports/VisitSummaryPdfReport.java:89`, `.../common/PatientDocumentsPrivilegeConstants.java:18`). OpenMRS creates privileges from the `<privilege>` entries in the module's `config.xml`, and that file had no entry for it. The sibling privileges were declared, but this one was missing, so the privilege did not exist in the database and could not be assigned to any role. The chart's print button gates on the same string with `UserHasAccess` (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-label-printing-app/src/print-visit-summary/print-visit-summary-action-button.component.tsx:35`), and a 403 from the backend is mapped to "not authorized" (`.../print-visit-summary.resource.ts:33-36`).

**The fix:** commit `9fc46c2cf8f6b7d3f2758379ac9b7af2d848b22a`, "Declare Visit Summary privilege in config.xml (#31)", adds the `<privilege>` entry with the description "Allows user to generate the visit summary PDF report." (`openmrs-module-patientdocuments/omod/src/main/resources/config.xml:55-58`). The diff is that one addition. The commit message and PR #31 don't reference a ticket key, and my searches didn't turn one up, so I can't name the ticket that tracked this bug.
